report:
**Conclusion: Yes.** High-quality randomized-trial evidence shows that denosumab (Prolia) reduces *new vertebral fractures* in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis.

The key evidence is the 3-year, randomized, placebo-controlled FREEDOM trial (7,808 women aged 60–90). Denosumab 60 mg injected every six months reduced new **radiographic vertebral fractures** from 7.2% with placebo to 2.3%—an absolute reduction of 4.9 percentage points and a **68% relative reduction**. It also reduced clinically apparent vertebral fractures (2.6% to 0.8%). Thus, the answer is not based merely on improved bone-density measurements; fractures were measured outcomes.

This evidence most directly applies to postmenopausal women with osteoporosis, especially those at elevated fracture risk. Professional guidance lists denosumab as an alternative initial treatment for high-risk postmenopausal women, but treatment must be maintained on schedule or followed by another osteoporosis drug: after stopping Prolia, bone loss is rapid and vertebral-fracture risk—including multiple vertebral fractures—increases.

Sources:  
- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19671655/  
- https://www.aafp.org/afp/2012/0215/p334.pdf  
- https://www.endocrine.org/clinical-practice-guidelines/osteoporosis-in-postmenopausal-women
